text:
mia chen: Heads-up — after landing the compact-tokenizer patch (commit f3a1b9) we're seeing an embedding drift on a subset of CJK/RTL evals. quick summary below.

raj patel: Ugh, what kind of drift? cosine on embeddings or generation BLEU/chrF?

mia chen: Both. embedding cosine similarity to baseline down ~0.08 avg for zh/ja testset; BLEU/chrF small but concentrated on honorifics/ruby/zwj boundaries. Also ar scripts show token count spike in some edgecases.

sophia nguyen: Do you have the exact command you ran? can we repro locally?

mia chen: Ran the standard bringup harness:

```
run_eval --model veridian-lite:v2 --tokenizer compact-tokenizer:v2 --quant q5 --locales zh,ja,ar --tasks embed,translate --seed 42
```

Got auto report from eval-bot (attached): embed_cosine_drop: 0.08; chrF_drop: 0.9; sample failure rate: 3.2%.

akira tanaka: My quick look — compact-tokenizer:v2 introduced a normalization step that collapses U+200B/ZWSP in pre-tokenization and also strips some combining marks when adjacent to kana/han. That could shift subword boundaries for ruby/furigana.

raj patel: That matches the token count spike in Arabic — maybe ZWJ/ZWSP handling changed mapping to explicit space vs removed char. Any diff of tokenizer mappings?

sophia nguyen: I looked at the tokenizer diff: https://git.internal/r/tokenizer/compare/f3a1b9..HEAD — a small normalization table was added plus a compacting pass that merges zero-widths into neighbors.

mia chen: repro scripts:

```
# reproduce minimal repro for embed drift
python -m evals.run --model veridian-lite:v2 --tokenizer compact-tokenizer:v2 --input tests/multilang/sample_zh_ja_ar.jsonl --mode embed --save outputs/embeds_v2.npy
python -m evals.run --model veridian-lite:v2 --tokenizer stable-tokenizer:v1 --input tests/multilang/sample_zh_ja_ar.jsonl --mode embed --save outputs/embeds_v1.npy
python -c "import numpy as np; print(np.mean(np.sum(outputs_v1*outputs_v2, axis=1)/(np.linalg.norm(outputs_v1,axis=1)*np.linalg.norm(outputs_v2,axis=1))))"
```

akira tanaka: I can bisect the tokenizer patch if needed. suspect culprit: compact-merge-zerowidth.

eval-bot: Automated bisect started by mia chen at 2024-09-15T14:12:34Z. Current candidate range: commits f3a1b9..f3a1b9 (single commit). Running sampler on 128 examples (zh/ja/ar).

mia chen: Plan: 1) validate that stable-tokenizer:v1 reproduces baseline, 2) bisect compact change, 3) check whether embedding kernel caused any numerical differences w/ q5 quant path. If tokenizer is root cause we'll try targeted fix (preserve ZWSP mapping, special-case ruby).

raj patel: I'll check quant kernel noise — small cosine shifts sometimes come from quantized matmul kernels when kvcache layout changes. I can run a determinism pass with float32 runtime to rule that out.

sophia nguyen: I'll own the tokenizer bisect + small patch if needed. assign to me, will update in 2-3 hrs.

mia chen: thanks. if you find a minimal failing example with furigana/honorifics that triggers BLEU/chrF drop, post it here. pinging @akira for locale edge cases. :pray:

akira tanaka: will do. quick note — include cases with ruby like: "漢字(かんじ)" and ones with ZWJ sequences in Arabic ligatures. those reproduce locally for me.

mia chen: perfect. once we confirm tokenizer is the cause we'll run a small onboard-to-dedicated smoke with quant q5 and float fallback to measure unit-cost impact.

eval-bot: Bisect update: commit f3a1b9 introduced compact-merge-zerowidth; reproducer failure rate 3.1% on sample. Suggest revert/soft-fix candidate: preserve U+200B and U+200D in pre-tokenize mapping.

raj patel: If preserving ZWSP fixes embeddings but increases token count marginally, we can suggest a selective preservation rule only for CJK/AR locales. tradeoff: +0.2 tokens per sample vs 0.08 cosine improvement.

mia chen: good tradeoff. Sophia, can you prototype locale-scoped rule?

sophia nguyen: Yup, I'll add locale guard in tokenizer and run the embed/translate eval suite. Will also add unit tests for ruby/zwj sequences.

mia chen: thanks all — please drop short notes here as you get results. we'll aim to ship a patch and re-run full regressions tomorrow morning. :rocket:
